$comment: Calendar quick add (meet#235): one typed sentence becomes an event draft, prefilled and not saved. One grammar, written twice — Sources/CalendarQuickAdd.swift and packages/contracts/src/quick-add.ts — and this file is what keeps them the same. `now` is the moment of typing, in `timeZone`; every `start`/`end` is local wall time in that zone (no offset written), or a YYYY-MM-DD day when `allDay`. `end` follows the default duration when the sentence names none. Anything the grammar does not consume is the title, with joining words and trailing punctuation trimmed. What it does not read — no date at all, or two time expressions — is what the Worker sends to the notes engine; `confidence` says which: 1 when a date and a time or an all-day span were read, 0.5 when only a date, 0 when nothing.
rules: TIME: 14:00, 14.00, 2pm, 2 pm, 9am, 14h, 14h30, 9:30am. A bare 1–12 with no marker is a time only inside a range or after 'at'.
RANGE: two times joined by '-', '–', 'to' or 'until' on the same day; a range end before its start is the next day only when the start is after noon (19:30-1:00).
DURATION: '45 min', '45 minutes', '1h', '1h30', '1.5h', '2 hours', 'for 30 minutes'. Sets end from start; ignored without a start.
TIME WITHOUT A DAY: today when the time is still ahead, otherwise tomorrow.

DAY: today, tomorrow, tonight (19:00 when no time), a weekday name (the next one, today included when the time is still ahead), 'next <weekday>' (the one after the coming one), 'on' before any of these is dropped.
DATE: '14 October', '14 Oct', 'October 14', 'Oct 14', '14/10' (day first), '2026-10-14'. Without a year: the next such date from today, today included.
SPAN: '3-5 Oct', '3 to 5 Oct', '3–5 October', 'Oct 3-5', '14 Oct - 16 Oct': an all-day event from the first day through the last; end is the day after the last, as Google stores it.
ALL DAY: 'all day' or 'all-day' anywhere makes the event all-day on its date, ends the next day; a date with no time and no span is a timed draft with no start time (the editor asks), not all-day.
LOCATION: 'at <words>' up to a comma, a time, a duration, a day, a date or 'with'; not when 'at' is followed by a time.

INVITEES: 'with <name>(, <name>)*( and <name>)?' where a name is one or two capitalised words; stops at a comma not followed by a capitalised word, a day, a date, a time, 'at' or 'for'. The names stay in the title too ('Lunch with Ana').

TITLE: the sentence minus every consumed span except the invitee phrase; commas, 'on', 'for', 'from' and 'the' left dangling at the edges are trimmed; internal whitespace collapsed. Empty title falls back to 'New event'.
RECURRENCE: 'every Monday' and the like are not read (meet#236 closed): the words stay in the title, the weekday inside them is not a date.
